title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 241
paragraphs: In my opinion he is also the cause that the air in these parts is dry, since he makes it so by scorching his path through the heavens; thus summer prevails always in the upper parts of Libya. If, however, the stations of the seasons had been changed, and where now in the heavens are placed the North Wind and winter were placed instead the South Wind and the midday, and where now is placed the South Wind there was the North — if this had been so, the Sun being driven from the middle of the heavens by winter and the North Wind would go to the upper parts of Europe, just as now he comes to the upper parts of Libya, and passing in his course throughout the whole of Europe I suppose he would do to the Ister what he now does to the Nile.
